questions.topicName: Histology of Blood Vessels and Lymphatics
questions.stem: This special-stained section shows abundant wavy, branching, dark-staining fibers running through the tissue. What extracellular component is being demonstrated?

explanation.summary: The wavy, refractile, dark-purple/black branching fibers are elastic fibers highlighted by an elastic stain (e.g., Verhoeff/orcein). Their recoil property underlies the elasticity of arteries such as the aorta.
explanation.whyCorrect: The wavy, refractile, dark-purple/black branching fibers are elastic fibers highlighted by an elastic stain (e.g., Verhoeff/orcein). Their recoil property underlies the elasticity of arteries such as the aorta.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Type I collagen forms thick, eosinophilic bundles that are pale with elastic stains and do not branch into fine wavy fibers.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Smooth muscle cells are cells with elongated nuclei and cytoplasm, not extracellular fibers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reticular fibers are fine type III collagen networks shown by silver stains, forming delicate meshworks in lymphoid organs rather than thick wavy fibers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fibrin forms in clots and on injured surfaces, not as an organized network of wavy fibers in normal tissue.

questions.stem: This vessel shows a thick, deeply eosinophilic wall of concentrically arranged smooth muscle surrounding a scalloped lumen, with a small nerve in the surrounding connective tissue. What type of vessel is this?

explanation.summary: The thick, smooth-muscle-rich tunica media and the wavy (scalloped) internal elastic membrane produced by contraction identify a muscular artery. The three tunicae (intima, media, adventitia) are clearly delineated.
explanation.whyCorrect: The thick, smooth-muscle-rich tunica media and the wavy (scalloped) internal elastic membrane produced by contraction identify a muscular artery. The three tunicae (intima, media, adventitia) are clearly delineated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lymphatic vessels have very thin walls with little or no smooth muscle, an irregular lumen and pale contents.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Large veins have a thin media and a thick adventitia with longitudinal smooth muscle, not a thick circular media around a scalloped lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Elastic arteries such as the aorta have many concentric elastic lamellae in the media, not a media mainly of smooth muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Capillaries are single endothelial tubes without a muscular wall.

questions.stem: Two small vessels lie side by side in this section; the left one has a relatively thick muscular wall for its lumen size while the right one has a thin wall and wider lumen. Which distinguishing feature identifies the left vessel?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A wall thickness large relative to its lumen

choices.label: B
choices.text: A single endothelial cell forming the whole wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: An outer layer thicker than the muscular layer

explanation.summary: Arterioles have a wall that is thick relative to their small lumen (one to a few smooth-muscle layers) to control resistance, whereas the companion venule has a thin wall and comparatively larger lumen.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arterioles have a wall that is thick relative to their small lumen (one to a few smooth-muscle layers) to control resistance, whereas the companion venule has a thin wall and comparatively larger lumen.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A wall formed by a single endothelial cell describes a capillary, not a vessel with a muscular wall.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Valves are found in veins and lymphatics, not arterioles, and the left vessel's distinguishing feature is its wall thickness.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A thick adventitia relative to the media is characteristic of veins, not of the muscular arteriole on the left.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fenestrated or discontinuous endothelium describes certain capillaries, not a vessel defined by smooth muscle layers.

questions.stem: This vessel has a very large, irregular lumen bounded by a strikingly thin wall with little smooth muscle. What functional property does this structure reflect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a low-pressure, high-capacitance conduit

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is the primary site of gas exchange

choices.label: C
choices.text: It generates the pulse pressure waveform

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a high-resistance flow regulator

explanation.summary: Veins have thin walls and large lumina and operate under low pressure, serving as capacitance (reservoir) vessels that hold much of the circulating blood volume. The thin wall cannot resist the high pressures seen in arteries.
explanation.whyCorrect: Veins have thin walls and large lumina and operate under low pressure, serving as capacitance (reservoir) vessels that hold much of the circulating blood volume. The thin wall cannot resist the high pressures seen in arteries.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Gas exchange occurs in capillaries, which have a single endothelial layer and a lumen about the width of one red cell, not a large irregular lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pulse pressure is generated by ventricular ejection into stiff, elastic arteries, not by thin-walled veins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: High-resistance flow regulation is the role of arterioles, which have a thick muscular wall relative to a small lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Withstanding high pulsatile pressure requires a thick muscular or elastic media, which this thin-walled vessel lacks.

questions.topicName: Histology of Blood Vessels and Lymphatics
questions.stem: Among the large clear adipocytes, a small vessel is highlighted whose wall is formed by little more than a single layer of endothelial cells. What is the chief functional role of this vessel?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Exchange of gases, nutrients, and wastes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Propulsion of blood by muscular contraction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Return of interstitial fluid to lymph nodes

explanation.summary: Capillaries consist essentially of a single endothelial layer and basement membrane; this minimal barrier is optimized for diffusion/exchange of O2, CO2, nutrients, and metabolic wastes between blood and tissue.
explanation.whyCorrect: Capillaries consist essentially of a single endothelial layer and basement membrane; this minimal barrier is optimized for diffusion/exchange of O2, CO2, nutrients, and metabolic wastes between blood and tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Propelling blood requires a muscular wall such as the heart's; a single endothelial layer cannot contract to pump.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lymphatic capillaries drain interstitial fluid, but this vessel lies in the blood circulation and its role is diffusion between blood and tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Blood storage is the role of large, compliant veins, not microscopic capillaries.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vascular resistance is regulated by arterioles with smooth muscle walls, which a single endothelial layer lacks.

questions.topicName: Histology of Blood Vessels and Lymphatics
questions.stem: This diagram compares three capillary architectures: one with an uninterrupted endothelium, one with pores through the endothelium, and one with gaps and a discontinuous basement membrane. Which type is characteristically found in the liver, spleen, and bone marrow?

explanation.summary: Sinusoidal capillaries have large intercellular gaps and a discontinuous basement membrane, permitting passage of cells and large proteins. They are found where such exchange is needed: liver, spleen, and bone marrow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sinusoidal capillaries have large intercellular gaps and a discontinuous basement membrane, permitting passage of cells and large proteins. They are found where such exchange is needed: liver, spleen, and bone marrow.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A postcapillary venule is a small collecting vessel downstream of capillaries and a site of leukocyte migration, not one of the three capillary types.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Continuous capillaries with an uninterrupted endothelium are typical of muscle, lung, skin and brain, not liver, spleen and marrow.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fenestrated capillaries with endothelial pores and an intact basement membrane are found in kidney glomeruli, endocrine glands and intestinal villi.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lymphatic capillaries are blind-ended drainage vessels for interstitial fluid, not part of the blood capillary bed of these organs.

questions.topicName: Histology of Blood Vessels and Lymphatics
questions.stem: This electron micrograph shows a small vessel whose lumen is enclosed by a single unbroken endothelial cell with an intact underlying basement membrane, surrounded by collagen and a muscle cell. Which capillary type is shown?

explanation.summary: An uninterrupted endothelial lining with a complete basement membrane and no pores defines a continuous capillary, the type found in muscle, nervous tissue, and skin, where it forms a tight, selective barrier.
explanation.whyCorrect: An uninterrupted endothelial lining with a complete basement membrane and no pores defines a continuous capillary, the type found in muscle, nervous tissue, and skin, where it forms a tight, selective barrier.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lymphatic capillaries have attenuated, overlapping endothelium with anchoring filaments and little or no basement membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Postcapillary venules are larger, with pericytes and a looser endothelium, and are the main site of leukocyte emigration.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fenestrated capillaries have pores through the endothelial cytoplasm, which are absent in this unbroken lining.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sinusoidal capillaries have wide gaps and a discontinuous basement membrane, unlike the intact lining shown.

questions.stem: This electron micrograph shows a red blood cell nearly filling a lumen lined by a single continuous endothelial cell with its nucleus bulging inward. What does this narrow luminal diameter, barely accommodating one erythrocyte, indicate about the vessel?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is an arteriole regulating resistance

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a capillary sized for single-file red cell passage

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a venule collecting deoxygenated blood

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a muscular artery with a contracted lumen

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is a lymphatic capillary draining tissue fluid

explanation.summary: Capillaries have lumina roughly the diameter of a single red blood cell, forcing erythrocytes to pass in single file. This slows flow and maximizes surface contact for efficient diffusion across the thin endothelial wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: Capillaries have lumina roughly the diameter of a single red blood cell, forcing erythrocytes to pass in single file. This slows flow and maximizes surface contact for efficient diffusion across the thin endothelial wall.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Arterioles have one or more layers of smooth muscle and a lumen larger than a single red cell.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Venules have wider lumina that hold several red cells, and their walls include pericytes or smooth muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Even a contracted muscular artery has a thick multilayered smooth muscle wall, unlike the single endothelial cell here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lymphatic capillaries normally contain lymph, not red blood cells, and have an irregular, often collapsed lumen.

questions.stem: This scanning electron micrograph of an endothelial surface shows numerous open pores and large gaps. What functional advantage do these openings confer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They permit passage of large molecules and cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: They increase resistance to blood flow

choices.label: C
choices.text: They prevent leakage of plasma proteins

choices.label: D
choices.text: They generate the vessel's contractile tone

choices.label: E
choices.text: They anchor smooth muscle to the endothelium

explanation.summary: Sinusoidal fenestrae are large openings in the endothelium (with discontinuous basement membrane) that allow proteins, and even whole cells, to move between blood and tissue, a property essential in liver, spleen, and bone marrow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sinusoidal fenestrae are large openings in the endothelium (with discontinuous basement membrane) that allow proteins, and even whole cells, to move between blood and tissue, a property essential in liver, spleen, and bone marrow.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Pores in the endothelium do not affect resistance to flow, which is set by vessel diameter and blood viscosity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Large gaps allow, rather than prevent, plasma proteins to cross the vessel wall.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Contractile tone comes from smooth muscle in the vessel wall, not from openings in the endothelium.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pores are openings in the endothelium, not anchoring structures, and sinusoids have no smooth muscle layer.

questions.topicName: Histology of Blood Vessels and Lymphatics
questions.stem: The vessel indicated by the arrow has an extremely thin, discontinuous wall and an irregular, collapsed lumen lacking red blood cells. What structural feature best explains how this vessel performs its physiologic role?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A thick tunica media of smooth muscle allows it to actively pump fluid

choices.label: B
choices.text: A complete internal elastic lamina lets it recoil and propel blood forward

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tight endothelial junctions restrict any movement of large molecules

choices.label: D
choices.text: A muscular valve system prevents contents from re-entering the interstitium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its endothelium has anchoring filaments and lacks a continuous basement membrane

explanation.summary: Lymphatic capillaries have a highly attenuated, overlapping endothelium with anchoring filaments and an absent/discontinuous basement membrane, permitting entry of interstitial fluid and macromolecules to form lymph.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lymphatic capillaries have a highly attenuated, overlapping endothelium with anchoring filaments and an absent/discontinuous basement membrane, permitting entry of interstitial fluid and macromolecules to form lymph.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lymphatic capillaries have no muscular media; lymph moves by tissue movement and the contraction of larger collecting lymphatics.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An internal elastic lamina belongs to arteries; this vessel has no elastic layer and carries no blood.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tight junctions would keep out macromolecules, the opposite of what lymphatic capillaries must allow in.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphatic capillaries rely on overlapping endothelial flaps acting as microvalves, not muscular valves; true valves appear in larger collecting lymphatics.

questions.topicName: Histology of Blood Vessels and Lymphatics
questions.stem: Two thin-walled vessels are shown side by side. What histologic feature most reliably distinguishes the lymphatic vessel from the accompanying vein in this section?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The lymphatic has a thicker, more muscular wall than the vein

choices.label: B
choices.text: The vein lacks an endothelial lining while the lymphatic has one

choices.label: C
choices.text: The lymphatic possesses a prominent internal elastic lamina absent in the vein

choices.label: D
choices.text: The vein contains valves whereas the lymphatic never does

choices.label: E
choices.text: The lymphatic lumen contains pale lymph, whereas the vein is packed with red blood cells

explanation.summary: Both vessels have thin walls, but the vein is filled with erythrocytes while the lymphatic carries clear, cell-poor lymph; this luminal content is the most reliable distinguishing clue on H&E.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both vessels have thin walls, but the vein is filled with erythrocytes while the lymphatic carries clear, cell-poor lymph; this luminal content is the most reliable distinguishing clue on H&E.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both vessels have thin walls, and lymphatics are generally thinner and less muscular than veins of similar size.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Both veins and lymphatics are lined by endothelium.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neither vessel has a prominent internal elastic lamina; that is a feature of muscular arteries.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphatics have numerous valves, more than veins, so the presence of valves cannot tell the vein apart.

questions.topicName: Histology of Blood Vessels and Lymphatics
questions.stem: This diagram shows the three concentric layers of a vessel wall. Which layer is chiefly responsible for actively regulating vessel diameter and thus blood pressure and flow distribution?

explanation.summary: The tunica media is composed of circumferential smooth muscle; its contraction and relaxation produce vasoconstriction and vasodilation, the principal determinant of vascular resistance.
explanation.whyCorrect: The tunica media is composed of circumferential smooth muscle; its contraction and relaxation produce vasoconstriction and vasodilation, the principal determinant of vascular resistance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The intima's endothelium releases vasoactive mediators, but the contraction that changes diameter comes from smooth muscle in the media.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The internal elastic lamina is a fenestrated elastin sheet that allows recoil but cannot actively contract.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The basal lamina is a thin extracellular sheet supporting the endothelium and has no contractile function.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The adventitia is connective tissue that anchors the vessel and carries vasa vasorum and nerves; it does not set diameter.

questions.topicName: Histology of Blood Vessels and Lymphatics
questions.stem: This vessel shows a strikingly wavy, refractile, brightly eosinophilic band at the luminal edge of the tunica media. What is the significance of this prominent single wavy lamina?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the endothelial lining of a large vein

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a well-developed internal elastic lamina, characteristic of a muscular artery

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is fibrin thrombus indicating acute vessel injury

choices.label: D
choices.text: It marks a lymphatic channel within the wall

explanation.summary: A single prominent, wavy internal elastic lamina between intima and media is the hallmark of a muscular artery; the waviness results from post-mortem smooth muscle contraction.
explanation.whyCorrect: A single prominent, wavy internal elastic lamina between intima and media is the hallmark of a muscular artery; the waviness results from post-mortem smooth muscle contraction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Endothelium is a thin cellular layer of flattened nuclei, not a thick refractile eosinophilic band, and large veins lack a prominent elastic lamina.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fibrin thrombus lies within the lumen as layered fibrin and blood cells, not as a regular wavy band between intima and media.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphatic channels are thin-walled lumens; they do not appear as a solid refractile band in the vessel wall.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Calcified plaque appears as purple, irregular deposits in a thickened intima, not a uniform wavy eosinophilic line.

questions.topicName: Histology of Blood Vessels and Lymphatics
questions.stem: Two accompanying vessels are shown in cross-section. Why does the artery retain a round, patent lumen with a thick wall while the companion vein appears flattened with a thin wall?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both vessels have identical wall thickness and the difference is artifactual

choices.label: B
choices.text: The artery is filled with lymph and the vein with blood

choices.label: C
choices.text: The artery has a thick muscular/elastic media to withstand high pulsatile pressure

choices.label: D
choices.text: The vein has a thicker tunica media than the artery

choices.label: E
choices.text: The vein carries higher pressure and therefore has the thicker wall

explanation.summary: Arteries have a thick, muscular and elastic wall to handle high, pulsatile pressure and keep a round lumen, while veins have thin walls and low pressure, so they collapse and appear irregular in fixed sections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arteries have a thick, muscular and elastic wall to handle high, pulsatile pressure and keep a round lumen, while veins have thin walls and low pressure, so they collapse and appear irregular in fixed sections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The difference reflects true structure: arteries have much thicker media than companion veins, not a processing artifact.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Arteries carry blood, not lymph; lymph flows in separate lymphatic vessels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Veins have a thinner media than arteries; their adventitia is the relatively prominent layer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Veins carry low-pressure blood, which is why they have thin walls and collapse in section.

questions.topicName: Histology of Blood Vessels and Lymphatics
questions.stem: This diagram contrasts a small artery and small vein. What is the functional role of the vasa vasorum shown in the adventitia of these vessels?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are lymphatic sinuses that drain the tunica intima

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are small blood vessels that supply the outer wall of large vessels

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are nerve endings that trigger vasoconstriction

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are the elastic laminae that provide recoil

choices.label: E
choices.text: They are valves that prevent backflow of blood

explanation.summary: The vasa vasorum ('vessels of the vessel') are small arterioles/venules that nourish the tunica adventitia and outer media of large vessels, whose walls are too thick to be supplied by luminal diffusion alone.
explanation.whyCorrect: The vasa vasorum ('vessels of the vessel') are small arterioles/venules that nourish the tunica adventitia and outer media of large vessels, whose walls are too thick to be supplied by luminal diffusion alone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lymphatics in the vessel wall exist, but the vasa vasorum are blood vessels supplying the outer wall, not sinuses draining the intima.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Perivascular sympathetic nerve fibers control tone; the vasa vasorum are small arterioles and venules, not nerves.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Elastic laminae are sheets of elastin in the intima and media, not small vessels in the adventitia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Valves are intimal folds within the lumen of veins, not small vessels in the adventitia.

questions.topicName: Histology of Blood Vessels and Lymphatics
questions.stem: This large vessel wall shows numerous parallel, wavy eosinophilic sheets distributed throughout a thick tunica media. What type of artery does this pattern identify, and what is the functional purpose of these sheets?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An elastic artery; the concentric elastic lamellae store energy in systole and recoil in diastole

choices.label: B
choices.text: A capillary; the sheets are basement membrane for filtration

choices.label: C
choices.text: A muscular artery; the sheets are smooth muscle that actively pumps blood

choices.label: D
choices.text: A small vein; the sheets are valves preventing backflow

choices.label: E
choices.text: An arteriole; the sheets regulate peripheral resistance

explanation.summary: Numerous concentric elastic lamellae throughout a thick media identify an elastic (conducting) artery such as the aorta; the elastin stores energy during systole and recoils during diastole (Windkessel effect) to maintain continuous flow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Numerous concentric elastic lamellae throughout a thick media identify an elastic (conducting) artery such as the aorta; the elastin stores energy during systole and recoils during diastole (Windkessel effect) to maintain continuous flow.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Capillaries are single endothelial tubes without a thick media, and their basement membrane is a single thin layer.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Muscular arteries have a media dominated by smooth muscle with one internal and one external elastic lamina, not many sheets; arteries do not actively pump blood.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Small veins have thin walls with little media, and valves are intimal folds within the lumen, not sheets in the wall.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Arterioles have only one to a few smooth muscle layers, not a thick media full of elastic lamellae.

questions.topicName: Histology of Blood Vessels and Lymphatics
questions.stem: This diagram of a tissue microcirculation shows arterial (red) and venous (blue) vessels linked by a capillary bed, plus a separate network of blind-ended green vessels weaving through the tissue. What is the primary function of the green vessels?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Perform gas exchange with tissue cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deliver oxygenated blood to the capillary bed

explanation.summary: The green blind-ended vessels are lymphatic capillaries. They collect excess interstitial (tissue) fluid, proteins, and cells not reabsorbed by the venous end of capillaries and return this lymph to the venous circulation, maintaining fluid balance.
explanation.whyCorrect: The green blind-ended vessels are lymphatic capillaries. They collect excess interstitial (tissue) fluid, proteins, and cells not reabsorbed by the venous end of capillaries and return this lymph to the venous circulation, maintaining fluid balance.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Gas exchange happens across blood capillaries, between the red and blue vessels, not in the blind-ended lymphatics.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Systemic vascular resistance is set mainly by arterioles with smooth muscle, not by lymphatic capillaries.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxygenated blood reaches the capillary bed through arterioles, the red vessels, not blind-ended green ones.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pulse pressure comes from ventricular ejection into elastic arteries; lymphatics are low-pressure, non-pulsatile drainage vessels.
